bullets.title: NVDA: BofA sees 34-50% undervaluation; bearish options flow & price-cut concerns weigh pre-earnings
bullets.body: BofA's sum-of-parts FCF analysis implies NVDA trades at a 34-50% discount to fair value, with AI risks overstated per the bank. Contrarian signal: options flow shows NVDA as the most bearish name today, Ben Thompson reports Nvidia is cutting prices via circular financing rather than list prices (margin pressure), and the Ohio data center commitment was slashed from $250B to $105B. NVDA earnings Aug 26 remain the next major catalyst; JPM sees the selloff as technical/low-volume rather than structural de-risking.

bullets.title: SNPS: Mizuho Outperform, $600 PT; FQ3 beat expected, agentic AI and Ansys synergies drive FY27 re-rate
bullets.body: Mizuho expects SNPS to beat FQ3 consensus ($2.44B revenue / $3.66 EPS) with IP growing high-single digits Y/Y and sequential improvement. Ansys integration targets ~$400M revenue synergies by FY27 within 3-4 years, potentially exceeding $1B longer-term. Agentic AI monetization adds a new three-tier pricing framework; Sept 30 Investor Day is a key catalyst. Stock down 23% since last earnings vs. IGV +10%, current price $413 vs. $600 PT.

bullets.title: META: -4.4% as 29-state youth addiction trial begins; down 16% YTD, worst year since 2022
bullets.body: Federal court trial commenced with 29 states alleging META deliberately designed Facebook and Instagram to harm children's mental health; prosecutors allege the company 'hooked and exploited' kids. META fell 4.4% on the session, is down 16% YTD, and has spent most of 2026 below its 200-day MA. JPM attributes the selloff also to off-balance-sheet financing scrutiny. One contrarian note: the stock trades at ~10x operating cash flow, reminiscent of 2022 lows.

bullets.title: FN: -19.4% on datacom softness despite Q4 beat; data center now 51% of revenue, guiding +43% growth
bullets.body: Fabrinet reported Q4 revenue of $1.316B (+45% Y/Y, above guide) and adj. EPS of $4.10, but NVIDIA-related datacom revenue fell 21% Y/Y, triggering the selloff. Data center revenue surged 68% Y/Y to $669M (51% of total). Q1 guidance of $1.375-1.425B implies ~43% Y/Y growth at midpoint, with new 800G hyperscaler-direct ramps beginning. JPM attributes the stock move to low summer volumes and notes it may not signal structural demand deterioration.

bullets.title: ANET: 40% 2026 revenue growth guided; 1.6 Tbps platform in trials, $20B AI networking market by 2030
bullets.body: At the Rosenblatt Technology Summit, Arista guided 40% revenue growth for 2026 with potential upside from supply improvement. The 1.6 Tbps platform is in customer trials with volume production targeted for 2027. Gross margins expected in the 60-64% range for 2027, operating margins 48-49% for 2026. Campus segment growing 45-50% in 2026; AI-driven Ethernet scale-up networking seen as a $20B market by 2030 with material ANET impact from 2028.

bullets.title: ARM: Cloud instance tracker shows +4% m/m, +41% y/y; Keybank views as positive alongside INTC, MU, NVDA
bullets.body: Keybank's Cloud Instance Tracker shows ARM processors surging +4% m/m led by Google Axion (+10% m/m) and AWS Graviton (+5% m/m), now +41% y/y. NVDA Blackwell instances +31% m/m to 333 total; INTC Granite Rapids +10% m/m to 4,145 instances. AMD flat m/m though Turin +4% m/m. Keybank rates the data positive for ARM, INTC, MU, NVDA; neutral for AMD.

bullets.title: AAPL: EU App Store overhaul effective Oct 1 — 26% in-app, 20% alternative payment, 5% out-of-app fee
bullets.body: Apple announced a restructured EU App Store fee regime effective October 1: 26% commission on Apple in-app purchases, 20% on alternative payment method apps, 15% on apps linking to external purchases, and a new 5% commission on out-of-app digital transactions (replacing the Core Technology Fee). Apple also added parental controls for under-18 users and expanded alternative marketplace access. Separately, US Congress is pressing Apple to pledge not to use Chinese memory chips.

bullets.title: SNDK: Up 62% from July lows on AI/datacenter NAND demand; mid-80s gross margins guided through 2030
bullets.body: SNDK is on a 6-day winning streak, up 62% since July's low, trading above 20/100/200-day MAs. IR notes datacenter is now the largest NAND consumer driven by AI inference; over half current LTA capacity utilized with two-thirds expected next year. Management is guiding mid-80s gross margins through 2030 and committed to returning 100% excess FCF via buybacks. Large tech deals now signed at CFO/CEO level rather than procurement.

bullets.title: HD: Mizuho raises PT to $390; Q2 comps +1.3% beat, tariff refunds boost EPS, digital sales +11%
bullets.body: Home Depot Q2 domestic comps came in at +1.3%, with 13 of 16 merchandising departments positive — best breadth since late 2022. Tariff refunds added ~$685M (~$0.30 EPS) to Q2 but only ~$45M expected in Q3, limiting upside. Digital sales +11% (5th consecutive double-digit quarter); SRS comps positive. Mizuho raises PT to $390; JPM models FY27 EPS of $16.54 vs. $16.08 street consensus with $398 PT. FY26 guidance maintained at +2.5-4.5% total sales growth.

bullets.title: DKNG: Michigan July sports betting GGR +32% Y/Y but handle share slips to 27% from 30%
bullets.body: Michigan July sports betting GGR rose 32% Y/Y for DraftKings, but handle market share fell to 27% from 30% a year ago, while FanDuel held share at 30%. DKNG's iGaming GGR grew only +3% Y/Y with market share declining to 17% from 20%. Hold rate improved +180bps to 12.6%, aided by promos at 4.4% of handle vs. 3.5% prior year. Morgan Stanley is also hosting a regulatory outlook event for US sports betting/iGaming on Aug 26.

bullets.title: GOOGL: Pixel supply chain shifting from China to Vietnam/India by 2027
bullets.body: Google is reportedly planning to move its entire Pixel smartphone, watch, and earbud supply chain out of China by 2027, with Vietnam and India as primary destinations, per Nikkei Asia. This is a supply chain diversification play consistent with broader tech de-risking from Chinese manufacturing.

bullets.title: TSLA: FCF deteriorating to -$9.7B in 2026; autonomy hype vs. 5-year underperformance debate intensifies
bullets.body: Multiple posts highlight TSLA's 5-year underperformance vs. NDX (+51% vs. +98%) and FCF swing from +$3.6B in 2021 to an expected -$9.7B in 2026 per Bloomberg. Bears argue Cybercab narrative lacks credibility and competitors will also solve autonomy. Bull case: Einride announced the largest public Tesla Semi commitment (500 trucks, first deliveries next month).

bullets.title: CRDO: Jefferies hosts NDR Sept 29, NYC; BUY rated at $270 PT on AI data infrastructure
bullets.body: Jefferies analyst Blayne Curtis rates CRDO BUY with a $270 PT (market cap $39.5B). The company provides high-speed copper and optical interconnect products including ZeroFlap active electrical cables up to 1.6T speeds. JPM also running a buyside survey seeking F1Q27 revenue/GM/EPS and F2Q27 guide expectations ahead of the Sept 1 report.

bullets.title: AMZN: Louisiana data center investment expanded from $12B to $18B with third campus
bullets.body: Amazon announced an increase in its Louisiana data center investment from $12B to $18B, adding a third campus. This reinforces the hyperscaler capex buildout narrative and comes alongside broader commentary that tech giants have ~$3T in off-balance-sheet AI-related spending commitments beyond reported capex figures.

bullets.title: DIS: ABC sues FCC over broadcast license review on First Amendment grounds
bullets.body: Disney's ABC unit filed a lawsuit against the FCC seeking to halt its early broadcast license renewal review proceeding, citing First Amendment concerns. No financial guidance impact disclosed; legal outcome could have longer-term regulatory implications for broadcast properties.

bullets.title: SPOT surges, CMCSA raises Peacock to $8.99/mo; media/streaming sector diverges
bullets.body: Spotify was a standout gainer in the Digital Media segment (+2.1% sector) while Peacock raised its Select plan minimum to $8.99/month after its first profitable quarter. META weighed on the Communications Services index (-0.6%) due to the youth addiction trial. NFLX contributed positively to Cable/Pay TV outperformance (+1.7%).

bullets.title: NNE, OKLO, GEV down on renewables sector weakness; AMRC downgraded at Baird
bullets.body: NNE fell 6.8% after signing an MOU with Quadrant Nuclear on HALEU fuel supply. Arcosa Renewables (AMRC) was downgraded to neutral from outperform at Baird with PT cut from $36 to $32, falling 10.6%. Hydrogen sector dropped 5.9%, solar -2.1%, wind -1.1%. GEV and BE also cited as weaker performers.

bullets.title: NVDA/MSFT confirm All-In Summit 2026 appearance; NVDA backs $105B SoftBank Ohio data center
bullets.body: Jensen Huang and Satya Nadella confirmed as All-In Summit 2026 speakers. Separately, NVIDIA confirmed it will back a 4.25GW SoftBank data center in Ohio valued at $105B (reduced from $250B per earlier reports), reinforcing AI infrastructure commitment but raising questions about the scale reduction.

bullets.title: DELL, HPE, SMCI: JPM hosting PC & server supply chain update call Aug 20
bullets.body: JPMorgan is hosting a PC and server market update call on August 20 at 8am ET with Asia Hardware analyst Albert Hung, discussing latest supply chain read-throughs to DELL, HPE, and SMCI. A separate JPM buyside survey is also tracking F2Q27 AI server orders/shipments/backlog and potential FY27 AI revenue raise expectations for DELL ahead of its Sept 3 earnings.

bullets.title: AAOI: Sold out, expects US production premiums for 800G/1.6T; cautious on LTAs to preserve optionality
bullets.body: At the Rosenblatt summit, AAOI noted it is currently sold out of all capacity. The company expects to receive premiums for US-produced 800G/1.6T components, positive for ASPs and margins. Management is deliberately cautious about signing long-term agreements to avoid blocking capacity for other customers, including NVDA.
